stories.headline: Two Nature papers show AI multi-agent systems succeed at validated drug-repurposing discoveries

key_facts.fact: Nature published two papers on May 19, 2026 describing AI multi-agent systems that help scientists generate and test hypotheses: Google's Co-Scientist and a system from FutureHouse.

Google's AI Co-Scientist proposed novel drug-repurposing candidates for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) that lab experiments validated, confirming the suggested drugs inhibit tumor viability at clinically relevant concentrations across multiple AML cell lines.

FutureHouse's multi-agent system Robin identified ripasudil, a ROCK inhibitor used for glaucoma, as a novel candidate for dry age-related macular degeneration; the team built Robin and made the discovery in just 2.5 months.

Both systems work in the background by orchestrating separate specialized tools and operate with expert-in-the-loop guidance across applications including drug repurposing, novel treatment targets, and antimicrobial resistance.

stories.headline: Alibaba's T-Head unveils Zhenwu M890 AI chip with annual upgrade cadence to rival Nvidia

key_facts.fact: Alibaba's chipmaking unit T-Head unveiled the Zhenwu M890 AI accelerator at an event in Hangzhou, China, on Wednesday May 20, equipped with 144GB of GPU memory, handling both training and inference and particularly suited to agentic tasks.
Alibaba now plans to upgrade its Zhenwu chip every year, accelerating to roughly the same pace as Nvidia.
The M890 delivers three times the performance of its predecessor, the Zhenwu 810E, and is purpose-built for AI agents that carry out multi-step tasks with limited human oversight.
Alibaba outlined a multi-year roadmap, with a successor chip called V900 in Q3 2027 (another ~3x gain) and a J900 in Q3 2028.
Alibaba Cloud presented a 128-card super-node server (Panjiu AL128) built on the M890 with an ICN Switch 1.0 interconnect chip, putting 128 accelerators into a single rack-scale machine.

stories.headline: Armada raises $230M Series B at $2B valuation, inks Johnson Controls factory deal for modular data centers

key_facts.fact: Armada raised a $230 million Series B round at a $2 billion valuation, announced Tuesday May 19; the round was oversubscribed and co-led by Overmatch, 8090 Industries, and BlackRock (a new investor).

Armada signed a manufacturing deal with Johnson Controls (which invested in the round) to build modular AI data centers at a new 400,000-square-foot Arizona factory called Galleon Forge One, expected to create more than 500 jobs.

The factory will initially produce Armada's Leviathan, a megawatt-scale data center, starting this summer; Armada's modular units can be deployed within days and run on local energy sources such as solar power and gas flares from oil wells.
Armada's modular data centers are already in use by customers including the U.S. Navy and remote offshore oil rigs; other new strategic investors include NightDragon, Mitsui and Singtel Innov8.

stories.headline: China bans imports of Nvidia's China-exclusive RTX 5090D V2 GPU, surprising the company

key_facts.fact: Chinese customs authorities imposed a complete ban on imports of the Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090D V2, the graphics card designed specifically for the Chinese market.
The decision came as a surprise to Nvidia and leaves Chinese gamers without the flagship card, forcing a switch to the cheaper model.
The RTX 5090D V2 was a downgraded export-compliant card with a 25% reduction in memory capacity and bandwidth (24GB on a 384-bit bus versus 32GB), kept at the same $2,299 MSRP.

stories.headline: Dell launches 18th-gen PowerEdge AI servers at Dell Tech World, with liquid-cooled AMD and Intel options

key_facts.fact: At Dell Technologies World in Las Vegas on May 19, Dell expanded its PowerEdge portfolio with eleven new servers and unveiled an 18th generation delivering up to 70% better performance and 13-to-1 consolidation via advanced air- and liquid-cooling designs.
The flagship liquid-cooled PowerEdge M9825 uses AMD EPYC 6th Gen processors in factory-integrated IR7000 racks for AI and HPC workloads; air-cooled R9825/R9815 reach up to 256 cores per system.

The new R9810 server uses Intel's next-gen 'Diamond Rapids' processor, doubling memory bandwidth and scaling up to 256 cores per socket (50% more than Granite Rapids); the M9825/R9825/R9815 ship in 2H 2026.

stories.headline: Google DeepMind to hire 20+ Contextual AI researchers in ~$90M licensing acqui-hire

key_facts.fact: Google DeepMind agreed to hire more than 20 researchers from startup Contextual AI and license its technology, a source told Reuters on Tuesday May 19, 2026; the deal was first reported by Bloomberg.
Alphabet paid between $80 million and $90 million to Contextual, and co-founder and CEO Douwe Kiela is among those moving to DeepMind.
The deal is the latest licensing-style acqui-hire by Google's parent; last year it paid $2.4 billion in licensing fees to use AI coding startup Windsurf's technology and hire several key staff.
Such acqui-hire tactics, used to sidestep US antitrust review, have drawn regulatory scrutiny as a 'red flag'; Contextual AI raised an $80M Series A in 2024 led by Greycroft.

stories.headline: Google launches Gemini 3.5 Flash as its 'strongest agentic and coding model yet' at I/O 2026

key_facts.fact: At Google I/O on May 19, 2026, Google introduced Gemini 3.5 Flash, positioned as its strongest agentic and coding model, now the default model in the Gemini app and Search AI Mode globally.
Gemini 3.5 Flash is priced at $1.50 per million input tokens and $9.00 per million output tokens (global), about 3x the per-token cost of the prior Gemini 3 Flash Preview.

Pichai said the model delivers frontier-level capability at less than half the price of comparable frontier models and runs four times faster on output tokens per second; he claimed top companies shifting 80% of workloads to 3.5 Flash could save over $1 billion a year.
On benchmarks, Gemini 3.5 Flash scored 76.2% on Terminal-bench 2.1 agentic terminal coding, 55.1% on SWE-Bench Pro, 83.6% on MCP Atlas, and 78.4% on OSWorld-Verified computer use.
Gemini 3.5 Pro, the heavier version, is being used internally at Google and will launch more broadly next month.

stories.headline: Google unveils Gemini Omni, a world model that generates video from any input

key_facts.fact: Google introduced Gemini Omni at I/O 2026, a multimodal model 'capable of generating samples in any output modality from any input,' starting with video and combining Gemini's intelligence with Google's generative media models.

The first model in the family, Gemini Omni Flash, is available starting today on the Gemini app, Google Flow and YouTube Shorts, with developer and enterprise API access coming in the following weeks.
Omni lets users edit video conversationally and create a custom AI avatar that looks and sounds like them; Google said users must complete a dedicated onboarding to prevent deepfakes.

Google framed Omni as part of its 'world model' push, moving AI from predicting text to simulating reality; a more advanced Omni Pro will follow with a claimed 'step change' in performance over Flash.

stories.headline: OpenAI co-founder Andrej Karpathy joins Anthropic to build a Claude-accelerated pretraining team

key_facts.fact: Andrej Karpathy, an OpenAI co-founder and former Tesla AI director, announced on Tuesday May 19, 2026 that he is joining Anthropic.
Karpathy posted on X: 'I've joined Anthropic. I think the next few years at the frontier of LLMs will be especially formative. I am very excited to join the team here and get back to R&D.'
Anthropic said Karpathy starts this week and will build a team focused on using Claude to accelerate pretraining research, working under head of pretraining Nick Joseph.
The hire signals Anthropic believes AI-assisted research is its primary strategy for staying competitive with rivals like OpenAI and xAI in a market where talent has become as valuable as compute.

stories.headline: Meta begins laying off ~8,000 employees as Zuckerberg accelerates AI overhaul

key_facts.fact: Meta began laying off roughly 8,000 employees, about 10% of its global workforce, with the first wave of notifications starting this week as part of an AI-driven restructuring.
Meta plans to transfer roughly 7,000 employees into new AI-focused groups including Applied AI Engineering, Agent Transformation Accelerator, and Central Analytics.
Meta is also shutting down plans to fill another 6,000 open positions; the company had nearly 78,000 employees (77,986) at the end of March.
Employees in North America were told to work from home as the cuts roll out; layoffs and transfers together affect about 20% of Meta's workforce.
The latest cuts bring Meta's total job reductions since late 2022 to nearly 35,000 employees.

stories.headline: Minnesota becomes first state to ban prediction markets; CFTC sues to block the law a day later

key_facts.fact: Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz signed SF 4760 into law on May 18, making Minnesota the first state to outright ban prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket; operating, hosting or promoting one becomes a crime as of August 1.

On May 19, the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Justice Department filed a lawsuit seeking to block the law, calling it a 'flagrant and unprecedented incursion' into the CFTC's exclusive jurisdiction over derivatives.
Minnesota is the sixth state the CFTC has sued over prediction-market crackdowns, after Arizona, Connecticut, Illinois, New York, and Wisconsin.

The Minnesota law has a broader reach than other state measures, criminalizing weather-related event contracts and targeting operators, payment processors, geolocation and data services across the prediction-market ecosystem; Kalshi was valued at $22 billion in a recent funding round.

stories.headline: Nvidia hand-delivers first Vera CPUs, its first custom CPU, to Anthropic, OpenAI, Oracle and SpaceX AI

key_facts.fact: Nvidia delivered its first Vera CPU systems to Anthropic, OpenAI, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and SpaceX AI, marking the chip's first customer rollout, with VP of hyperscale and HPC Ian Buck personally handing them over at California sites.

Vera is Nvidia's first custom CPU, purpose-built for agentic AI workloads, with 88 custom Olympus cores, 1.2 TB/s of memory bandwidth and per-core performance 50% faster under full load than comparable designs.

Vera is part of the Vera Rubin NVL72 platform, pairing with Nvidia GPUs over NVLink-C2C at 1.8 TB/s coherent bandwidth (7x PCIe Gen 6); SpaceX AI is evaluating Vera for reinforcement learning applications.

stories.headline: Sam Altman offers every YC startup $2M in OpenAI tokens in exchange for equity

key_facts.fact: Late Tuesday May 19, 2026, Sam Altman offered to invest $2 million in every startup in the current Y Combinator batch — paid not in cash but in OpenAI tokens.

Altman unveiled the offer in a talk to YC founders and posted on X: 'I am excited to see what will happen with tokenmaxxing startups, both for how they work internally and the products they can build.'

The token investment gives early-stage AI startups cost-free access to advanced models for rapid prototyping while positioning OpenAI as both investor and infrastructure provider in the startup ecosystem.

stories.headline: OpenAI launches Guaranteed Capacity, selling 1-3 year compute commitments with volume discounts

key_facts.fact: On Tuesday May 19, 2026, OpenAI announced Guaranteed Capacity, letting customers secure long-term access to compute for products, agents and workflows via 1-, 2- or 3-year commitments with discounts that increase with annual commitment.
Customers can draw down the committed spend across OpenAI's product portfolio and use guaranteed allocations across supported cloud providers and model families.
Sam Altman called it a 'big win-win' for planning ahead, said OpenAI will offer it until current allocation sells out, and that the company will ensure enough capacity remains for ChatGPT and Codex.
OpenAI positioned the offering as a way to help customers plan ahead 'in a compute-constrained world.'

stories.headline: Samsung Electronics union to launch 18-day strike May 21 after bonus talks collapse

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics' labor and management failed to reach an agreement Wednesday in last-ditch government-mediated talks, and the unions said they will launch an 18-day strike starting Thursday May 21.
The union said it agreed to the National Labor Relations Commission mediation proposal around 10pm on May 19, but management refused.
Around 50,500 workers are set to walk off production lines for 18 days; the dispute centers on a bonus cap and demands to allocate 15% of operating profit to bonuses.

A Suwon District Court on Monday partially granted Samsung's injunction to block a full strike, so minimum staffing will be maintained, but supply disruptions are still expected at the world's largest memory chipmaker.

South Korea's government has signaled it may invoke emergency arbitration powers, which would suspend industrial action for 30 days while the NLRC conducts binding arbitration; industry estimates of losses if the strike proceeds run to 20-30 trillion won.

stories.headline: Singapore signs National AI Partnership with Google and OpenAI MoU; OpenAI commits S$300M for first overseas lab

key_facts.fact: Singapore announced separate agreements with Google and OpenAI on May 20, including a new National AI Partnership with Google and the first MoU between Singapore and OpenAI, led by the Ministry of Digital Development and Information.

OpenAI committed more than S$300 million (about US$234 million) to Singapore's AI ecosystem and will open its first Applied AI Lab outside the US there, growing technical teams to more than 200 roles over the next few years.

The 'OpenAI Singapore Applied AI Lab' is the first such lab established outside the US and will support work in public services, finance, healthcare and digital infrastructure; most of the 200+ hires are forward-deployed engineers.

Google's deal did not include an investment figure and focuses on healthcare, education and scientific research; the partnership builds on Singapore's broader strategy committing over S$1 billion to public AI research from 2025 to 2030.

organizations: Ministry of Digital Development and Information

stories.headline: Malaysia's SkyeChip surges nearly 300% on Bursa Malaysia chip-design IPO debut

key_facts.fact: SkyeChip's share price nearly quadrupled on its Main Market debut on May 20 to RM3.50, up 297.7% above its 88 sen IPO price.

The company raised RM352 million from the IPO, issuing 400 million new shares representing 22.3% of its enlarged share capital, with proceeds going mainly to R&D, computing infrastructure, EDA tools and working capital.
The IPO drew overwhelming retail demand with 74,453 applications for 3.45 billion shares under the Malaysian public tranche.

Penang-based SkyeChip is a fabless IC design firm specializing in licensable silicon IP and custom ASICs with access to 3nm process node technology, positioning Malaysia to move up the semiconductor value chain into front-end design.

stories.headline: FTC begins enforcing Take It Down Act, requiring platforms to remove nonconsensual intimate images within 48 hours

key_facts.fact: On May 19, the Federal Trade Commission began enforcing Section 3 of the Take It Down Act against platforms that fail to comply with notice-and-removal requirements, after a one-year grace period expired.
Covered platforms must remove nonconsensual intimate images — real or AI-generated 'digital forgeries' — along with known identical copies within 48 hours of a valid request.

Platforms that fail to comply face civil penalties of $53,088 per violation; covered platforms include Meta, Snapchat, TikTok, X, Reddit, Discord, Pinterest, Bumble, Match Group, Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft.

stories.headline: Trump signs EO ordering Fed and regulators to review fintech and crypto access to payment rails

key_facts.fact: President Trump signed an executive order on May 19 directing the federal government to integrate digital assets and fintech firms into traditional financial services and payment systems, and to remove regulations that primarily benefit incumbent firms.

The order directs heads of financial regulators to review existing rules within 90 days and asks the Federal Reserve to evaluate frameworks governing access to Reserve Bank payment accounts and services by non-bank financial firms.
It marks the first explicit White House directive instructing evaluation of direct access to Reserve Bank payment accounts for non-bank crypto firms.
Trump signed a separate order the same day directing Treasury to issue guidance on banking services to illegal immigrants and consider Bank Secrecy Act changes to strengthen customer identification.

stories.headline: Trump says he was 'an hour away' from ordering Iran strike before Gulf states convinced him to pause

key_facts.fact: On May 19, Trump told reporters at the White House he was 'an hour away' from deciding whether to attack Iran on Tuesday before being convinced to postpone the strike for a few days.

Trump said leaders of Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE asked him to hold off because 'serious negotiations' were taking place; he gave Iran a limited window of two or three days, possibly until early next week.
A strike would have ended the shaky US-Iran ceasefire that remains nominally in place; Iran submitted a revised 14-point peace plan to Washington through Pakistani mediation.

Per CNN, Gulf states warned that resuming bombing would invite Iranian retaliation against their energy infrastructure, and several signaled they may restrict US use of air bases and airspace if Trump proceeds.

stories.headline: White House draft AI EO would set voluntary framework for labs to share frontier models with government before release

key_facts.fact: Sources told Axios the White House plans to release an executive order on cybersecurity and AI safety as soon as this week, with two main sections: cybersecurity and 'covered frontier models.'

The draft calls for a 'voluntary framework' under which AI labs would share their models with the government at least 90 days before public release and also give access to certain critical infrastructure providers.

The cybersecurity component aims to secure the Pentagon and national security agencies, boost cyber hiring, protect systems at hospitals and banks, and encourage breach threat-sharing between the AI industry and government.

organizations: Center for AI Standards and Innovation
